expired_window.result: The first mailing request failed before enrichment, embedding or model work. The attempt produced no edition or model receipt.

sources.manifest_definition: Each row is an expected paper in one seven-day collection. arXiv rows record the first new or cross entry in the Physics group during the window, the exact v1 identifier, submission date and subject tags from the versioned Atom query. The text digest is SHA-256 over the whitespace-normalized title, a newline and the whitespace-normalized abstract. APS rows are papers with CC BY rights and an abstract in the dated Physical Review A or B Harvest inventory. The membership comparisons use the source records before deduplication.

sources.interpretation: A subject can repeat a cross-listing of an existing paper. Membership and day are evaluated separately from subject metadata. For 2608.25540 the Atom v1 record named gr-qc as primary and the human-readable v1 landing page named hep-th. Both included the same three subject codes. DataCite update timestamps are recorded as publisher deposit metadata and are not used as first mailing dates.

editorial_protocol.reviewer: Codex checked the hosted decisions against the authors’ research papers and publisher records.
editorial_protocol.ranking_sample: Upper halves round up. Alternate September 2 and October 14, then use September 30 only for vacant places. Take high ranks downwards and low ranks upwards. Deduplicate by exact paper membership. Each initial week had fewer than ten ranks.
editorial_protocol.exclusions: Three wholly rejected detailed proposals and two wholly rejected initial candidates per initial week. Order within each review stage by SHA-256 of sorted paper IDs joined by a newline. Incomplete decisions and rank caps do not count as rejections.
editorial_protocol.judgments: Compare each original ranking and its English headline, brief and synthesis with the primary literature, including full paper sections for disputed scope, attribution and missing subsets. A proceedings report summarizing prior work can share a physical question while failing the original-contribution eligibility rule. Companion studies with distinct new measurements or calculations are eligible. The measurements assess the original copy before reader corrections. The initial decision target is nine passes per group of ten.

ranked_source_coverage.unit: Distinct supporting paper at an active rank, assigned once to its primary arXiv subject or APS journal. Cross-listings and the two overlapping next-day editions are excluded from this count. An arXiv primary can be outside the 18 tracked subjects.

case_reviews.original_headline: Exact-m_c NNLO update gives SM B→X_sγ rate (3.54±0.14)×10^-4 for E_γ>1.6 GeV
case_reviews.proposed_question: SM prediction of the inclusive B→X_s γ branching ratio (E_γ>1.6 GeV) and its comparison with the experimental average. The three papers share the same value, (3.54±0.14)×10^-4, so they are companion or overlapping results from the same calculation, not independent replications.
case_reviews.assessment: The works address exactly the same inclusive radiative branching ratio, but Huber's conference proceedings recapitulate previously published calculations. Section 5 explicitly attributes both calculations to earlier work. The other two papers give the technical calculation and its phenomenological analysis. The digest counts the report toward the minimum of three original contributions and assigns it new calculation work. Its exclusive claim about the charged-Higgs bound also fails against equation 17 of the proceedings.
case_reviews.withdrawal: Two papers supply an original calculation and its phenomenological analysis. The third is a conference report on prior calculations and also presents the same charged-Higgs mass bound. This set contains fewer than three original contributions.

case_reviews.original_headline: DESI BAO-based H0 values range 62–71 km/s/Mpc depending on calibrator and model choices
case_reviews.proposed_question: H0 constraints from DESI BAO (DR1 angular or DR2) combined with other late-universe or low-redshift probes (SNe/chronometers, BBN prior, FRBs)
case_reviews.assessment: All three analyses infer the Hubble constant with DESI acoustic-distance information. The numerical estimates and named priors agree with the papers. The synthesis calls all three calibrators late-universe or low-redshift probes. The second analysis uses an early-universe baryon-density prior from primordial nucleosynthesis.

case_reviews.original_headline: Simulated decoders match or beat BP+OSD on surface, bicycle and lifted-product codes
case_reviews.proposed_question: Logical error performance of BP-based/message-passing decoders on surface, bivariate bicycle or LP codes versus the BP+OSD baseline
case_reviews.assessment: All three benchmark logical decoding error against belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding. The digest identifies code families, noise models and the simulated setting. The neural decoder's 0.2% figure refers to computational complexity. It is kept separate from its decoding accuracy.

case_reviews.original_headline: Schwarzschild deformations shift ISCO and shadow; NLED dyonic model shrinks the ISCO
case_reviews.proposed_question: How a deformation of the Schwarzschild geometry changes the ISCO radius and related orbital/shadow quantities in specific or generic modified spacetimes
case_reviews.assessment: All three calculate the innermost stable circular orbit for a perturbed Schwarzschild spacetime. Kazempour and Sun also compare the shadow with Sgr A* data. The Letelier study fits oscillation frequencies under its stated precession model. Hohenegger develops a response expansion for orbital and shadow observables. The copy distinguishes that calculation from the observational fits.

case_reviews.original_headline: New methods map transport and current fluctuations in exclusion processes and XXZ chains
case_reviews.proposed_question: Nonequilibrium transport and current/activity fluctuation characterization in driven or dissipative lattice models, covering classical exclusion processes and open quantum XXZ chains
case_reviews.assessment: The exclusion-process paper counts every hop, including opposing hops. Its conclusion identifies directional current statistics as future work. The quantum generating-function paper tracks transferred charge, and the noisy XXZ paper computes current counting statistics. The digest's headline extends the current result to the exclusion-process analysis.
case_reviews.withdrawal: One paper counts every particle jump in a classical exclusion process. The other two calculate net charge transfer or current in quantum chains. Opposing jumps add to activity and cancel in a net current. The classical paper identifies directional current statistics as future work, leaving two papers for the claimed current comparison.

case_reviews.original_headline: Flat-ΛCDM lensing H0: 65.0 from SN Refsdal vs 71.1 from TDCOSMO quasars with Ωm prior
case_reviews.proposed_question: H0 from strong-lens time-delay cosmography in flat LCDM, reported as value and percent uncertainty (lensed supernova and lensed quasar samples)
case_reviews.assessment: Schuldt and colleagues infer H0 from a lensed supernova using a specified cluster mass model. The other two papers report the same eleven lensed quasars, including the matter-density prior. The English gives the two estimates and uncertainties and correctly identifies the companion publications.

case_reviews.original_headline: Calculations suggest light-hole character boosts Ge hole-spin qubit control, coupling
case_reviews.proposed_question: Whether LH or HH-LH mixed character improves the electrical spin-control or coupling performance of Ge hole spin qubits compared with HH character
case_reviews.assessment: All three model how light-hole admixture changes electrically driven spin response in germanium qubits. The copy attaches the isotropic response, the Rabi-frequency and coherence trade-off, and the cavity figure of merit to their respective calculations. It identifies the device proposals as theoretical.

case_reviews.original_headline: Proofs of α→1 continuity of regularized channel Rényi divergence give strong converses
case_reviews.proposed_question: Continuity at α=1 of the regularized sandwiched Rényi channel divergence and the resulting exponential strong converse for simple channel-pair discrimination
case_reviews.assessment: The four preprints tackle the same order-one limit and its consequence for discriminating a pair of quantum channels. The brief's dates are the September 24 and 25 Physics announcements. The synthesis attributes the distinct proof methods and finiteness assumptions to their authors. Zhu and Wang explicitly extend the result to general testers and identify their exponent.

case_reviews.original_headline: Endothermic dark matter models confronted with LZ's single 248 keV xenon recoil candidate
case_reviews.proposed_question: Whether a specific endothermic/inelastic dark matter scenario reproduces the 248 keV xenon recoil, with its kinematic parameters or predictions
case_reviews.assessment: Four groups calculate different endothermic scenarios for the same single LZ recoil. Each contributes a new model calculation. The brief distinguishes the excluded parameter region of the primordial-black-hole model from the other benchmark predictions. The experimental paper confirms the recoil energy and its two reported uncertainties. The gamma-line estimate is conditional on radiative decay.

case_reviews.original_headline: Model-based tests of binary black hole formation channels against GW populations
case_reviews.proposed_question: Constraining the relative contribution or viability of formation channels using gravitational-wave data or population-level predictions (triples, isolated, dynamical)
case_reviews.assessment: All three compare black-hole formation scenarios with gravitational-wave observations. The triple-star simulations account for several low-mass population features, the event fits test component-spin priors, and the population model infers channel efficiencies. The digest attributes the comparable channel fractions to the third model and describes mass-ratio reversal as a proposed pathway.

case_reviews.original_headline: Model calculations give polarization-split in-medium φ properties and ρ00<1/3 in holographic models
case_reviews.proposed_question: Polarization-resolved in-medium φ properties (transverse vs longitudinal splitting and resulting φ spin alignment ρ00 relative to 1/3) from in-medium spectral calculations
case_reviews.assessment: All three treat the polarization-resolved in-medium response of the same phi meson. The sum-rule study separates transverse and longitudinal masses. The two spectral models also derive spin alignment and differ on its sensitivity to density. The synthesis correctly limits the spin-alignment ratio to the two holographic calculations.

case_reviews.original_headline: Optimizer vs Adam in VQCs: SPSA costlier; QNG lead cost-model dependent; Riemannian no gain
case_reviews.proposed_question: Whether a given optimizer beats Adam or other baselines in cost or accuracy when training variational quantum circuits
case_reviews.assessment: The three groups benchmark optimization of parametrized quantum circuits. Wei compares circuit-evaluation costs, Belozerova tests energy error and success on hydrogen chains, and Cotea evaluates objectives on several workloads. Cotea includes Adam updates and distinguishes hardware case studies from the simulator ranking. The synthesis keeps those conditions attached.

case_reviews.original_headline: Dust masses from RSG winds, LRD analogs and a WC binary differ by orders of magnitude, by method
case_reviews.proposed_question: Dust masses produced by individual stellar or stellar-like source classes (RSG winds, LRDs, WC binary) and their contribution to the dust budget
case_reviews.assessment: The three papers estimate source-associated dust mass in solar units. The red-supergiant model predicts wind condensates, the Wolf–Rayet study infers dust formed in an outburst, and the little-red-dot analysis estimates total dust reservoirs. Photometry does not establish how much of those reservoirs formed in the outflow. The synthesis opens by calling all three values dust formed. The systems also differ, so the numbers cannot isolate a measurement-method effect.
case_reviews.corrected_excerpt_from_original: dust mass formed by individual source classes

case_reviews.original_headline: Inelastic dark matter models tested against the LZ high-energy recoil candidate
case_reviews.proposed_question: Whether a specific inelastic dark matter model can explain the high-energy LZ recoil candidate while satisfying the solar-neutrino, mediator or other constraints
case_reviews.assessment: The three theory teams ask whether the same high-energy recoil can be accommodated by their dark-matter candidates, then test different additional constraints. The surviving fractions, solar limits and mass ranges are attributed to the appropriate benchmarks. All three interpret the existing LZ observation.

case_reviews.original_headline: T→P leakage vs r~1e-3: BICEP3 measured residual, CGEM and LiteBIRD simulated
case_reviews.proposed_question: Size of T→P leakage bias on r (or relative to r~1e-3) in a CMB polarimeter and how it is controlled/mitigated (deprojection, optical design, instrument requirements)
case_reviews.assessment: The papers all evaluate instrumental temperature-to-polarization contamination in microwave-background measurements. BICEP3 measured its detector beams and used them in timestream simulations to estimate residual leakage. The headline presents the residual itself as measured. CGEM separately observed its beam on the sky, while the LiteBIRD paper simulates coupled instrumental effects.

case_reviews.original_headline: Gauged U(1) models fit LZ's single 248 keV recoil candidate as inelastic dark matter
case_reviews.proposed_question: Inelastic DM models that explain the LZ 248 keV event and define compatible parameter space
case_reviews.assessment: All three test distinct gauge models against the same LZ event. The quoted recoil energy and maximum local significance agree with the detector collaboration. The account identifies one event and treats subsequent constraints and gravitational-wave signals as model-dependent predictions. Rank 5 also interprets this event with different papers.

case_reviews.original_headline: Companion SN 2025wny analyses derive H0 from time delays, conditional on lens model
case_reviews.proposed_question: Measured H0 from time delays of the lensed supernova SN 2025wny, combined with lens models. The papers share the target and the delay and lens-model data, so they are companion analyses rather than independent replications.
case_reviews.assessment: The three companion papers contribute spectroscopy, photometry and lens modelling of the same supernova. Each provides a distinct original measurement or model. The summary gives their H0 constraints under the named lens assumptions and identifies the shared observations.

case_reviews.original_headline: Models and inverse design of time-varying metamaterials for frequency and momentum conversion
case_reviews.proposed_question: Modeling or design of time-varying metamaterials and metasurfaces for scattering and frequency/momentum conversion; shared author name only, no evidence of common data or replication
case_reviews.assessment: The common physical question is how time variation controls scattering into different frequencies. In the cylinder model the wavevector is conserved even when the direction of energy transport changes. The multilayer design also produces distinct momentum channels. The synthesis says a shared author name is the only stated connection, although the two manuscripts name the same coauthor and department at Aalto University.
case_reviews.corrected_excerpt_from_original: A shared author name is the only stated link

case_reviews.original_headline: Reduced quantum-algorithm energies versus classical references: Ru fragment, H8 chain, benzene dimer
case_reviews.proposed_question: How closely a reduced/quantum-algorithm electronic-structure energy reproduces a classical reference energy (truncation or emulation error) for a given system
case_reviews.assessment: The three studies calculate an electronic energy and quantify its agreement with a classical reference. Each numerical value is tied to its system, basis or comparator. The hardware check for the hydrogen chain is an energy difference, distinct from the emulated self-consistent-field energy. The benzene result is the interaction minimum for the stated basis.

case_reviews.original_headline: Theoretical quantum-battery charging: protocol and control parameters set stored energy, each in its own model
case_reviews.proposed_question: Charging performance and stored energy of quantum batteries as a function of charging protocol and control parameters
case_reviews.assessment: All three calculate how controllable parameters affect a quantum battery's energy. The antiblockade enhancement, distance threshold for two emitters, and double-dot ergotropy belong to separate models. The synthesis identifies theory throughout and preserves the distinction between stored energy, charging efficiency and extractable work.

One contribution establishes time complexity for forward ordinary-differential-equation evolution. Barthe proves truncation convergence and treats posterior-state preparation. An and colleagues instead test classical parameter recovery from a quantum loss for inverse problems. The latter two share an inverse-problem setting, but all three lack a common output or physical benchmark.

The angle-resolved spectra demonstrate electronic replica bands, ptychography measures layer-resolved atomic relaxation, and the trilayer calculations predict relaxed domains and topological bands. The reconstruction study and simulation share structural observables. The large-angle bilayer experiment attributes its replicas to interlayer scattering and supplies a different observable.

All three studies use TESS light curves to measure pulsation periods or frequencies in delta Scuti stars. The catalogue supplies population period and amplitude distributions and the two high-amplitude samples resolve the modes of individual stars. A comparison can retain the shared authors and TESS provenance and distinguish population evidence from individual mode identifications.

The gadolinium study predicts atomic-ion emission lines. The other two address tetraquark radiative properties and resonance poles. The particles, measured quantities and spectra differ, leaving fewer than three comparable works.

The first group separates ultrafast spin and orbital pumping currents, the second measures interface spin-to-charge conversion, and the third calculates torques exciting particular magnon modes. Sharing a magnetic interface does not supply a single conversion efficiency or magnon yield across the three.

Two papers examine transitions between extended and localized single-particle states. The qudit paper instead locates a many-body ergodicity threshold as a function of local Hilbert-space dimension. The network paper measures spreading and Shannon entropy across topologies. The three lack a common localization threshold or transport comparison.

The condensate study reports scaling of single-parameter Fisher information near dynamical saddle points. The trapped-ion proposal evaluates weak-field sensitivity with detuned squeezing and short interrogation. The level-crossing study targets simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters against a Holevo bound. Their sensitivities refer to different tasks and resource measures.

Aditi and Becker construct intervals for state fidelity. Köhne and colleagues estimate circuit fidelity decay versus depth. Porta-San Miguel and colleagues certify whether a logical circuit error rate falls below a threshold. These outputs cannot support one three-study estimate of fidelity or error.

Three teams directly measure stellar rotation periods from cyclic emission. The radio and optical ultracool-dwarf periods agree near 3.079 hours. The KIC red-giant analysis measures a 35.515-day spot period, and the xi Persei team obtains a 2.040514-day period from spectroscopic and photometric variability. The red-giant result is in the primary paper's period analysis. The maser and wind papers need not enter the comparison.

The condensate study predicts bistability in matter-wave transmission, the lattice-clock experiment measures spectroscopic linewidth and coherence time, and the photonic proposal predicts gravitationally induced phase and visibility changes. Interferometry alone supplies no common measured quantity for the three works.

interpretation: The two historical date pairs measure incremental model charges and source turnover. They do not increase the count of observed live operating dates. Replicate notifications can occur in subject mailings. Several topic groups draw on the same observing campaign or candidate, and the publication decision also considers the number of distinct original contributions.
decision: Expanded Physics remains on demand while the editorial targets and 14 shared live-cost dates are outstanding. The public Physics edition covers four arXiv subjects. The owner will select the service-wide monthly budget after measured pilots.

recurring_claims_reviewed_in_adjacent_ed.headline: SM B→X_sγ branching ratio (3.54±0.14)e-4 for Eγ>1.6 GeV agrees with experimental average

verdict.assessment: The headline changed while all three first-version sources remained identical. The following day’s synthesis recognized the conference report as a recap but still attributed part of the calculation to it and claimed that only the phenomenological analysis derives the mass bound. Equation 17 of the report gives that bound. There are two original contributions.
verdict.withdrawal: Two papers supply an original calculation and its phenomenological analysis. The third is a conference report on prior calculations and also presents the same charged-Higgs mass bound. This set contains fewer than three original contributions.
